data/cards/2611.25179.json and data/cards/2611.26969.json — this week's cards (full text read 2026-11-22 by the card stage); every robotics number here is theirs with its table or section named
export.arxiv.org API, four calls 2026-11-22 (abstracts of 2609.37771, 2606.00985, 2608.30536, 2303.07280, 2512.23703 read from the responses)

import_sentence: In statistical physics a one-bit macroscopic description of a many-body state is a block-spin coarse-graining, valid only when the partition it induces is lumpable (the chance of leaving the 'success' block must not depend on which microstate inside it the system occupies) and robust only to the microscopic perturbations that are irrelevant (whose effect on the coarse variable shrinks as the coarse-graining scale grows); carried into L5, that says a benchmark success checker $c : \mathcal{X} \to \{0, 1\}$ is that block-spin map, its persistence window $\tau$ and spatial tolerance are the coarse-graining scale that the shipped first-hit readout sets to zero, SimAudit's phantom successes (a stack falling within 60 ms, a gripper bit true one physics step after the open command, a contact reported across a 2 cm air gap, a policy credited for stopping) are non-lumpable microstates inside the success block, RoboDyna's 5-12% latency flips are a perturbation whose relevance is undecided because no repeat-run floor was measured, and the principled test for which checker variables and which simulator settings (time step, contact offset, latency) matter to the recorded bit is the excess flip rate $\psi_j(\tau)$ against the window: decaying to the repeat floor means irrelevant at that readout, flat or growing means relevant.

predicts.statement: Setup. RoboTwin 2.0 in SAPIEN at its released physics configuration (the step is not stated in 2611.25179; read from the released config and printed), the 10 tasks where SimAudit says the flips concentrate ('4 to 19 of the 50 tasks ... largely the same tasks for every policy', App. E; the task list comes from the released counterexamples), two released policies ($\pi_{0.5}$ Motus checkpoint and X-VLA, the two with the largest RoboTwin flip shares, 5.6% and 4.7%, Table 2), 40 official seeds per task, every episode run to the time limit with the episode never terminated at first hit, the full simulator state logged at every physics step, both the original checker $c$ and SimAudit's released Verified checker $c'$ evaluated offline on the log. Arms, each the same seeds: A0 and A0' two runs at the shipped setting $\theta_0$ (the repeat null); A1 physics step halved, $h \to h / 2$, control interval unchanged (two substeps per control tick); A2 contact offset doubled, $d_c \to 2 d_c$; A3 RoboDyna's operator ported, the scene advanced by the measured forward-pass time $\Delta_n$ before each chunk executes ($\delta = 1$) against the paused default ($\delta = 0$). Quantities. The windowed verdict $C_\tau^{(i)}(\theta) = \mathbf{1}[\exists\, t \le T - \tau : c(x_s) = 1\ \forall s \in [t, t + \tau]]$ for episode $i$ at setting $\theta$, for $\tau \in \{0, 60\,\mathrm{ms}, 250\,\mathrm{ms}, 1\,\mathrm{s}, 3\,\mathrm{s}, T\}$ ($\tau = 0$ is the shipped readout, $\tau = 1\,\mathrm{s}$ is $c'$'s window, $\tau = T$ is the terminal-state reading RoboDyna uses); the flip rate $\phi_j(\tau) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbf{1}[C_\tau^{(i)}(\theta_0) \ne C_\tau^{(i)}(\theta_j)]$ over the $N = 400$ paired episodes per policy; the null $\phi_0(\tau)$ from A0 against A0'; the excess $\psi_j(\tau) = \phi_j(\tau) - \phi_0(\tau)$; the exponent $y_j = -\, \mathrm{d} \ln \psi_j(\tau) / \mathrm{d} \ln \tau$ fitted over the four nonzero windows, positive meaning irrelevant; the same flip rates under a spatial tolerance scan (checker region and contact-distance thresholds multiplied by $\{0.5, 1, 2\}$) to separate time-type from space-type operators; and the per-episode escape time $e^{(i)} = \min\{s > t^\ast : c(x_s) = 0\} - t^\ast$ after the first hit $t^\ast$, whose distribution inside the success block is the lumpability check (true successes have $e = \infty$ to the time limit; phantom microstates have $e$ in the tens of milliseconds). P1 (time operators are irrelevant by one second): $\psi_h(0) > 2$ pp on at least 5 of 10 tasks and $\psi_h(1\,\mathrm{s}) < 1$ pp on at least 7 of 10, so $y_h > 0$. P2 (the air-gap operator is a space operator): the flips SimAudit attributes to 'pressing without touching' (Table 4: 6 / 23 / 20 / 24 / 19 per policy, the largest group) are flat in $\tau$ and fall by at least half when the contact-distance threshold is halved. P3 (latency is relevant where the scene moves): $\psi_\delta(\tau) > 3$ pp at every $\tau$ including $T$ on the tasks with a moving or falling object, and under 1 pp on the static ones. P4 (the null): $\phi_0(0)$ is between 1 and 4 pp (policy sampling noise plus chaotic contact; SAPIEN CPU PhysX is repeat-identical, so the null is the policy's) and falls below 1 pp at $\tau = 1\,\mathrm{s}$. P5 (lumpability): the escape-time distribution inside the success block is bimodal with a mode under 100 ms whose mass equals SimAudit's phantom share for that policy (3.3-10.2% of original successes, Table 2) within 2 pp.
predicts.expected: Judgment, not evidence: probability 0.45 that P1, P2 and P3 hold together (the window sorts the operators: step and transient defects irrelevant by one second, air-gap contact a space operator, latency relevant on dynamic tasks), with P4 and P5 at 0.6 each independently. Mechanism expected: a halved step changes contact impulses and penetration depths at the millisecond scale, which decides whether a first-hit checker fires one tick early or late but not where the object rests one second later; a doubled contact offset changes which air-gap distances the engine reports as contact, which the window cannot remove but a contact-force condition does; latency changes which state the policy acts on, so on a moving scene the object ends elsewhere and every readout scale sees it. SimAudit's own Table 4 is the prior for P1 and P2: transient success (2 / 9 / 13 / 11 / 15 flips per policy) and command-based grasp (0 / 0 / 5 / 3 / 7) are removed by its one-second window, while 'pressing without touching' (6 / 23 / 20 / 24 / 19) needed a force condition.
predicts.field_assumes: Three stated positions. (i) The evaluation protocol: benchmarks end the episode at the first checker hit ('The benchmark ends the episode at the first state on which the checker returns success and records a success', 2611.25179 sec. 3.1) and pause the world during inference (RoboDyna sec. I on the frozen-world regime), so the success bit is treated as the macroscopic variable at $\tau = 0$ and the numerics as fixed infrastructure; under this $\psi_h \approx \psi_{d_c} \approx 0$ at every window including zero. (ii) SimAudit treats the one-second persistence as a repair ('require the conditions to hold for one second', sec. 3.3) and validates it on 1,233 expert episodes at one simulator setting; the window is never scanned and never crossed with a physics setting. (iii) RoboDyna reads 85 / 63 / 34 changed outcomes of 700 as latency sensitivity ('This paired evaluation isolates the effect of inference latency', sec. II-C) with no sync-sync repeat, that is $\phi_0 = 0$ assumed; and the engine-comparison register (Manda 2026-10-05, read for CL-W46-07) says coarse outcomes are step-robust while force peaks are not, with no policy and no checker.
predicts.belief_changing: Two results, either one changes a ruler. (a) The floor is the signal: $\phi_0(\tau)$ is 3-6% at $\tau = 0$ and does not fall with $\tau$ on the contact-rich tasks, so the recorded success bit is not a slow variable of the simulator at any readout scale, SimAudit's 3.1-5.6% and RoboDyna's 4.9-12.1% are the same repeat floor measured twice, every paired flip count in this register needs the null printed beside it, and no checker repair at fixed settings removes it; the lane's repeatability claim (CL-W43-09, killed on its training framing) returns as an evaluation fact. (b) The time step is relevant at the one-second window: $\psi_h(1\,\mathrm{s}) > 3$ pp on at least 3 of 10 tasks, so the Verified checkers are repaired at one setting only, checker validity cannot be certified without naming the numerics, and CL-W46-07's reporting rule (print the step and a sensitivity row) extends from Scores to checkers. Also belief-changing in the other direction: if $\psi_\delta$ decays to the floor by $\tau = 1\,\mathrm{s}$ on every task, latency is an irrelevant operator for these benchmarks' verdicts and RoboDyna's flips are first-hit timing, which closes its headline and the lane's latency scout together.

identifiability: Random given: fixed policy checkpoint, fixed task set and official seeds, fixed checker code (original and Verified, both evaluated offline on the same logged states so the two checkers never see different episodes), fixed simulator build; the only thing that varies between paired arms is the named setting $\theta_j$, and the only thing that varies between A0 and A0' is nothing named, which is what makes A0 vs A0' the null. Whose temperature: the policies sample ($\pi_{0.5}$ and X-VLA are flow-matching; whether their noise is seedable is unknown, not in either card), so $\phi_0$ is the policy's decision variance plus whatever the simulator does not repeat; SAPIEN CPU PhysX repeated identically three times in the engine comparison read for CL-W46-07, so the expectation is that the null is the policy's, and the probe reports the null with the noise seeded and unseeded if the harness allows it. The checker is deterministic code evaluated on a logged state; there is no judge anywhere (SimAudit's VLM reviewer is not used; the lumpability check reads escape times from the log). Whose property: relevance is a property of the triple (task, checker, setting pair) at a stated window, not of the policy alone and not of the simulator alone; the headline names the levels ($h$ shipped vs halved, $d_c$ shipped vs doubled, $\delta \in \{0, 1\}$ at the measured forward-pass time on named hardware) and the window set, because a variance share is design-dependent (checklist 2026-11-01) and a relevance verdict read at one window is a protocol statement until the window is scanned. Chaos is in the conditioning set: contact dynamics amplify any perturbation, so an unstructured perturbation of the same size as the structured one flips some episodes too; that is exactly why the structured arm is read against the repeat null and not against zero, and why 'relevant' is defined as excess over the floor that persists with the window rather than as a nonzero flip count. Judge versus verifier: the recorded bit is a verifier output; the Verified checker is a second verifier; the lumpability check is a property of the simulator's own transitions and needs neither.

cheapest_probe.design: Step 1 (3 days, no GPU): install RoboTwin 2.0 and SimAudit's released checkers and counterexamples; pick the 10 flip-concentrated tasks from the released RoboTwin flip lists; write the harness that disables first-hit termination, logs the full state at every physics step, exposes $h$, $d_c$ and the RoboDyna latency operator (scene advanced by the measured forward-pass time before each chunk), and evaluates $c$ and $c'$ offline at any window and tolerance. Step 2 (about 70 GPU-hours, 4 days, one GPU for inference with the CPU simulator): 5 arms (A0, A0', A1, A2, A3) x 2 policies x 10 tasks x 40 seeds = 4,000 episodes run to the time limit, about one minute each. Step 3 (2 days, no GPU): the window scan, the tolerance scan, $\phi_j(\tau)$, $\phi_0(\tau)$, $\psi_j(\tau)$, $y_j$ with seed-cluster bootstrap intervals, the escape-time distribution inside the success block per policy, and a reconciliation against SimAudit's Table 4 repair types. Step 4 (optional, about 15 GPU-hours, 1 day): if RoboDyna's checkpoints and seeds are released, the sync-sync repeat of $\pi_{0.5}$ on the 700 matched pairs, which gives its headline the floor it lacks and tests P3 on physically moving scenes. Trigger to park at step 1: SimAudit's release (checkers, flip lists) is not public by the start date, or RoboTwin's harness cannot be run past first hit without changing the physics (then the probe moves to RoboCasa365 with the same design).
cheapest_probe.dollars: about $250 at $3 per GPU-hour, or $0 on an owned GPU; the simulator is CPU and the analysis is offline
cheapest_probe.days: 10 days: 3 of harness, 4 of runs, 2 of analysis, 1 for the optional RoboDyna arm
cheapest_probe.kills_if: Dead as a ruler if every excess $\psi_j(\tau)$ is within 1 pp of zero at every window for every operator (nothing is distinguishable from the repeat floor; the operators do not move the verdict and CL-W46-07's one-knob table is the whole story), or if every $\psi_j(\tau)$ is flat in $\tau$ including the transient-success defects SimAudit's own window removed (the readout scale organises nothing and the relevance picture adds no information to a sensitivity table). Dead as a claim if $\psi_h(0) < 1$ pp and $\psi_{d_c}(0) < 1$ pp on at least 8 of 10 tasks (the numerics are irrelevant to the verdict already at the shipped readout; the checker's defects are code alone, as SimAudit assumes, and the import reduces to its one-second window). Both outcomes are citable: the first as the null every paired flip count needs, the second as the sentence that closes the numerics question for first-hit checkers on RoboTwin.

consumers.class: Benchmark owners and checker authors (RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, RoboDojo, LIBERO family, Genie Sim, Behavior-Skill's per-skill success conditions)
consumers.action_changed: Print each checker's persistence window and tolerance as a stated readout scale, ship the window at which the numerics become irrelevant instead of first hit, and add the escape-time check (mass inside the success block under 100 ms) to the checker regression suite.

consumers.class: Evaluation-protocol authors who report paired flip counts (RoboDyna, Reflex / ReflexBench, SimAudit's re-scoring, SIMPLER-family real-to-sim tables)
consumers.action_changed: Report the repeat-run floor $\phi_0$ beside every changed-outcome count and label each setting relevant or irrelevant at the stated window, so a 5-12% flip count is read as excess over a floor rather than as a sensitivity.

papers.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
papers.trick: Have an LLM read a benchmark's task instruction and its success-checker code separately, stage the states where the two disagree in the unmodified simulator, and re-score released policies' rollouts with the repaired checker.
papers.did_not_do: Its Verified checker is a coarse-graining at one scale ('require the conditions to hold for one second', sec. 3.3) applied as a repair and validated at one simulator setting; the window is never scanned, never crossed with the physics step, contact offset or latency, and the simulator is held fixed throughout ('this paper holds the simulator fixed and audits the checker instead', card neighbours). Its re-scoring has no repeat null (the same rollouts are scored twice, so $\phi_0 = 0$ by construction and the simulator's own non-repeatability is never measured). It states the lumpability failure in words and leaves it ('A policy that goes on to release is therefore credited early, and a policy that stops there is credited for a task it did not finish. The recorded episode is the same in both cases', App. C) without measuring escape times inside the success block; its 'pressing without touching' group is a contact-reporting artifact of the engine ('a contact point that the simulator reports across an air gap of up to 2 cm', App. E) that it repairs in the checker rather than reading as a simulator-setting operator.

papers.title: Faster and Better? Benchmark Bugs and Design Limitations Distort the Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Acceleration
papers.trick: Start from tasks where an approximation of a policy scores above the policy, plot object trajectories against the checker's acceptance regions, and find 22 bugs and 4 design limitations across seven benchmarks whose fixes reverse method rankings.
papers.did_not_do: Names both operator types in one sentence, 'success criteria and simulation settings do not fully capture how acceleration affects task execution' (abstract, API), and treats them separately: it tightens permissive checkers (the spatial tolerance) and corrects object masses, with no time step, contact offset or latency arm (CL-W46-07 kill record: zero mentions of time step, solver or Hz), no window scan, no repeat null, and the checker and the setting never crossed. Third: 2611.26969 RoboDyna (card) measures one operator, latency, at one window (the terminal state) with no repeat null and no other setting. Fourth: 2610.41857 (card neighbour) reruns a shipped benchmark with one physics parameter changed (mass, solver iterations, depenetration velocity, contact time constant) with frozen policies and the checker fixed, and reads the success rate, not per-episode flips against a window. Fifth: Kaedim 2610.00731 (CL-W46-07 record) prints the numerics (240 Hz, 6 mm contact offset, 64/16 iterations) in a validity table and holds them fixed. Sixth, ours: CL-W46-07 is a one-knob Score-shift table on Genie Sim at a fixed readout with a repeat floor; this import differs by making the checker's readout scale the independent variable, defining relevance as excess over the floor that survives the scale, and reading the lumpability of the success block from escape times.

nearest_existing_use.verdict: Not made. The coarse-graining in the robotics checker literature exists at exactly one scale, as a repair (SimAudit's one-second persistence; 2609.37771's tightened regions), and the simulator-setting sensitivity exists at exactly one readout, as a success-rate shift (2610.41857, Kaedim, Manda, CL-W46-07) or as a paired flip count without a floor (RoboDyna). No fetched source scans the window, reads a setting's flip rate against the window, subtracts a repeat null, or names relevant and irrelevant operators for a success checker; the field-word conjunction (Q1) returns no robotics checker paper at all, and the RL-abstraction conjunction (Q3) returns none. It is not a rename of the W44 S3xF11 import (compaction graded by the relaxation time of kept entries, Mori-Zwanzig memory, Chapman-Kolmogorov composition, for L4 messages): the object here is the scorer and the simulator state, the field tools are block-spin relevance and Kemeny-Snell lumpability rather than implied timescales, and the quantity is a flip rate against a readout scale under a setting perturbation, not a memory kernel of a summary. It is not a rename of CL-W46-07 (Score shift under one knob at a fixed readout). Two-year density: 43 in-window hits across four queries, two on point, both from the last eight weeks; race window judged 2-3 months against a 10-day probe, with the SimAudit authors (released checkers and flip lists) and the 2609.37771 authors (trajectory-versus-region tooling) as the natural first movers.
